newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Bank selloff, energy news move Hungary's OTC market.
newsitem.headline: Bank selloff, energy news move Hungary's OTC market.

text.p: Bank shares have stolen the show on the Hungarian over-the-counter (OTC) market, traders said, adding that the market as a whole still lagged behind the bourse despite some revival in the past few days.
"The bourse now receives more attention," said Peter Tatar of IBB Securities.
Activity was mixed in the electricity utility shares after the government last week postponed the energy price hike to January 1, 1997 from October 1, 1996.
Former trader expectations that privatisation news would move bank shares were confirmed recently.
"On news that the privatisation of Magyar Hitel Bank approaches its price firmed to around 80 to 85 percent of the face value from around 70 percent," Attila Hunyadi of Buda-Cash Brokerhaz Kft said.
Hunyadi saw unlikely MHB's price to strengthen substantially after newspaper information that the bank's privatisation will occur at or below face value.
Budapest Bank's price has strengthened to around 78 percent on talks that its shareholder, the U.S.'s General Electric Group, was buying additional stocks.
MKB bank shares traded at around 16,000 to 17,000 forints.

Trading was slump in electricity utility Edasz Rt, while another utility firm Demasz Rt has weakened to around 35 to 36 percent of the face value or 3,500 to 3,600 forints on what Hunyadi attributed to the fact that speculators lost patience.
Unlike Demasz, other regional electricity utilities, Dedasz Rt and Titasz Rt have strengthened, while Emasz Rt has virtually no activity.
Titasz has risen to around 40 percent of the face value or 4,000 forints from 35 percent, while Dedasz rose to around 50 percent from around 40 to 45 percent.
"It's worth to buy these shares at 40 to 50 percent of face value even if the energy price increase is postponed to next year," Hunyadi said.
"Rumours circulate around Demasz and Titasz that the strategic investors show interest in buying more share packages," Hunyadi said.
"These rumours triggered interest of speculators, too."
Under Hungary's electricity privatisation process, Germany's Bayernwerk AG bought 47.25 percent in Dedasz, while a 49.23 percent stake in Titasz was sold to the German Isar-Amperwerke AG.
Preference stocks strengthened in parallel with the rise on the bourse of ordinary shares of the same companies, they said.
"Shares which have direct link with the bourse, such as Richter and OTP have moved," said Tatar. "Buying intention firmed for both."
